## Real-data mosaic development preview

The first mosaic increment joins two small windows from actual downloaded DEMs
at their existing source grid. `launch_terrain_mosaic_trial()` calls
`fluvgeo::mosaic_terrain_tiles()` in a separate process, using native terra merge
with explicit first/last-valid source precedence and no resampling. This path
does not call the horizontal-warp primitive described below.

An explicit `fgstudio.mosaic_trial` option supplies the small real-data fixture
when developing the producer. `terrain_mosaic_trial_ui/server()` now also renders
saved DEM editions in ordinary sessions under Survey Events, after Event settings,
with the saved Reach boundary and tile boundary. No development option is needed
to reopen a saved result. Current editions cover a portion of a Reach, not a full
Stream DEM; the publication and download path is described below.

The masking increment uses `launch_terrain_mask_trial()` and
`fluvgeo::mask_terrain_mosaic()` to apply a small window of the existing saved
Reach mask. The source and saved Event horizontal grids already match, so no warp
or resampling is needed. The original full compound CRS and metre elevation units
are retained. Horizontal component comparison allows the DEM's compound CRS and
the mask's 2D CRS without relabeling either input.

The masked trial is displayed only for its matching Study Area and Survey Event.
The real source declares NAVD88 metres; the saved target is NAVD88 international
feet. The current trial uses `launch_terrain_feet_trial()` to call
`fluvgeo::terrain_to_international_feet()`: native terra division by exactly
0.3048, retaining NoData, Float32 storage and the horizontal metre grid. Output
vertical CRS is EPSG:8228; no datum transformation occurs. The conversion does
not change the saved vertical specification. The saved mask grid
is reused without establishing a new initial-grid convention.

Trace `R/terrain_mosaic_trial.R` and `tests/testthat/test-terrain-mosaic-trial.R`.
The backend contract is `fluvgeo/dev/schemas/terrain-tile-mosaic.md`; opt-in
testthat inputs are small real DEM windows. Unknown vertical compatibility and
the future target-grid convention are not resolved by a same-grid trial.

## Horizontal warp primitive

`fluvgeo::warp_terrain_horizontal()` is an existing backend primitive; there is no
current FG Studio caller or new analyst approval step. It takes a source GeoTIFF,
a template defining the output grid, and a new output directory. Template values
are not applied as a mask.

The implementation uses native GDAL warping with an explicit horizontal pipeline
and `-novshift`. This option matters: the installed GDAL control test converts
compound US-survey-foot heights to metres under a default warp to a 2D metre CRS.
The guarded operation preserves the height units and retains source declarations.
It does not perform a vertical transformation or certify source suitability.

Aligned grids use nearest sampling; other grids use bilinear interpolation.
Float32 is the storage default and Float64 is optional. GDAL chooses working
precision and memory settings. Native terra summaries replace custom R block
traversal and the broken deleted-helper dependency. Exact sample comparisons
remain in small independent tests, not a second exhaustive production audit.
There are no application cell-count, row-width or estimated-disk admission caps.

GDAL handles affine source rotation and unequal spacing. Ordinary overviews are
allowed, but analytical warping uses base pixels to avoid inheriting an unknown
overview resampling method. The output template must be north-up. The retained
operation profile supports static east/north projected CRSs with the same identified
geodetic base; datum/epoch changes, nonidentity scale/offset and external
georeferencing/mask sidecars still need explicit implementation. These are API
scope boundaries, not universal GIS restrictions.

Trace sibling fluvgeo `R/warp_terrain_horizontal.R`,
`tests/testthat/test_warp_terrain_horizontal.R` and
`dev/schemas/horizontal-terrain-warp.md`. Tests retain independent interpolation,
NoData, unit-conversion controls, crop/extension and wide-grid cases. Source and
output hashes, metadata, native summaries and software/options are recorded before
the final manifest is written. No shared library is upgraded.

Stream/Event mosaic assembly remains unimplemented. Compatible neighbouring tiles
need the intended overlap rule and interpolation support before warping, followed
by the saved Stream mask. The unmounted [source-review module](dev-14-source-review.html)
is not a manual approval prerequisite for current mask creation. Remediating this
primitive does not authorize new vertical operations or establish the scientific
compatibility of all source DEMs.

## Combined real-window worker

`R/terrain_dem_trial.R` now connects the three existing backend primitives in one
worker: `mosaic_terrain_tiles()` -> `mask_terrain_mosaic()` ->
`terrain_to_international_feet()`. The opt-in trial starts automatically for its
matching saved Study Area and Event. It offers cancellation, retry after failure,
and reuse of completed output based on its recorded local input recipe. There
are no intermediate approval buttons. Edits, a changed Event or session closure
stop pending work before cleaning its unique staging directory. Tests use the
existing real Reach fixture and mock process handles for lifecycle assertions.
The normal mask display is disabled; optional `fgstudio.mask_diagnostics` is only
for development troubleshooting. The feature design owns cache details and limits.
This is still a small Reach development path, not full Stream/Event publication.

## Saved output and normal app sessions

`local_study_store()` includes the `study_dem_store()` adapter from
`R/study_dem_store.R`. `terrain_dem_trial_job()` can stage output in the Study
store and call `publish_dem()` after saved binding/input checks. Completed cached
output is copied in a worker rather than recalculated. A directory rename publishes
an immutable edition; cancellation cleanup cannot remove a published edition.

`terrain_mosaic_trial_server()` now also serves saved DEMs in ordinary sessions,
without development fixture options. The Survey Events card shows saved status,
explicit **Reach portion** scope, a map and **Download DEM (GeoTIFF)**. Reopening
checks the edition record and file size, without raster scans. Developer options
still control the small-area builder; this does not enable full Stream assembly.
Trace `tests/testthat/test-study-dem-store.R` and the app contract
`dev/schemas/survey-event-dem.md`. The local binding includes the saved Study,
Event and collection selection; stale editions are excluded from current output.
